name: Evaluación de la Ley: Evaluating Laws in Chile (Briefing Note)
content:
## Evaluación de la Ley: Evaluating Laws in Chile

**Location:** Chile
**Implementation Level:** National

### Overview
Evaluación de la Ley (Law Evaluation) is a program run by the Chilean Chamber of Deputies' Law Evaluation Department to assess the real-world impact of legislation after it has been passed. The program uses citizen focus groups to gather evidence on how laws are working in practice.

### How It Works
The Chamber of Deputies' Law Evaluation Department staff are trained to run citizen focus groups to evaluate the impact of legislation. This community-led evidence gathering provides lawmakers with direct feedback on whether laws are achieving their intended outcomes.

### Key Features
- Trained staff facilitate citizen focus groups to evaluate enacted legislation
- The process focuses on the evaluation stage of the lawmaking cycle — after laws have been passed
- Uses community-led evidence gathering to assess real-world legislative impact

### Lessons Learned
- Evaluating laws after enactment is an important but often overlooked stage of the lawmaking process
- Training public servants to facilitate constructive citizen engagement is essential for high-quality participation
- CrowdLaw can be applied at every stage of the legislative cycle, including post-enactment evaluation
